claims.claim: Highest-priority next improvement: turn `verifier_ledger` into a repair loop. Today the verifier writes unresolved citation/lineage issues to state and disk, but the next-round agent prompts never include those issues, so agents can only keep guessing until `max_rounds`.

The convergence detector is still not fully trustworthy against polite-agent false convergence. `detect_convergence` still treats empty `disagreed_with_peer` plus peer-claim coverage in `agreed_with_peer` as the positive signal; the ledger only vetoes unresolved citations or lineage flags, not substantive capitulation.

Required `evidence_path` makes findings syntactically inspectable, not semantically falsifiable. The verifier resolves files and extracts snippets, but it never checks whether the snippet actually supports the claim, and `PositionEvidence.content_snippet` is defined yet unused by verification.

The shipped deliberation chassis is structurally pair-only, not genuinely N-agent. CLI parsing, builder validation, and verifier peer-mapping all assume exactly two agents, so the topology cannot add a third substantive perspective where shared blind spots would matter most.

For `max_rounds > 5`, the first structural stress is more likely convergence drift plus terminal synthesis bloat than budget exhaustion. Per-round agent prompts stay bounded to peer-latest plus own-prior, and budget enforcement is trace-cumulative, but synthesis serializes the full `position_history` and agents never receive cumulative verifier state.

Asymmetric duet plus symmetric deliberation is a sensible base partition, but it is missing a third pattern: judge-guided audit/repair. Duet has reviewer-gated revise/block routing for implementation work; deliberation has symmetric peers plus a passive verifier; nothing currently routes independent adjudication back as required obligations.

evidence.content_snippet: "converged" if round >= 2 and every agent's latest position has an empty ``disagreed_with_peer`` AND covers every claim ID the peer last emitted in ``agreed_with_peer``
evidence.label: Convergence Contract

evidence.content_snippet: Prompt includes "Peer's most-recent position" and "Your prior position (last round)" before the Position schema; no verifier ledger section is added.
evidence.label: Next-Round Prompt Inputs

evidence.content_snippet: return {"verifier_ledger": [e.to_dict() for e in new_ledger.entries], "prior_positions_by_agent": next_prior}
evidence.label: Verifier State Output

evidence.content_snippet: A resolvable citation returns status="verified" with file_path, line_range, snippet, and notes; no claim-to-snippet truth check occurs.
evidence.label: Semantic Verification Gap

evidence.content_snippet: `PositionEvidence` defines `label`, `citation`, `content_snippet`, but `verify_position` only walks `claims` and `disagreed_with_peer` evidence_path values.
evidence.label: Unused Evidence Payload

evidence.content_snippet: "Deliberation v1 requires exactly 2 agents; got {len(pair)}. N-agent (≥3) is a future extension"
evidence.label: Exactly Two Agents

evidence.content_snippet: The smoke tests assert only that the schema is accepted by real providers, not that citations are truthful or disagreements are substantively resolved.
evidence.label: Schema Smoke Scope

open_questions: Should the next fix be a new adjudicator node that emits unresolved obligation IDs, or should the existing verifier node own that contract directly?
If three-agent support lands, should the third participant be another substantive debater or a dedicated skeptic/judge role?
reviewer_summary: Ranking by leverage: (1) add verifier-feedback obligations to the next-round prompts and convergence state, (2) stop treating self-reported agreement as sufficient convergence evidence, (3) tighten semantic citation verification or actually consume `PositionEvidence`, (4) only then generalize to 3-agent, (5) optimize long-round synthesis/drift. The single highest-priority improvement is the obligation loop because it reuses the shipped verifier, directly reduces bogus-citation loops, makes polite false convergence harder, and gives long debates a stable memory of unresolved issues instead of forcing agents to infer why convergence did not fire.
